motivation: Depth and sediment alone did not explain persistent site state. Tampa Bay seagrass ecology and management identify underwater light at depth as a mechanistically plausible constraint on Thalassia condition.

source_inputs.event: Pinned TBEP Darwin Core Event table at commit 6c567beff95ea04f0e397101befb49d5233ace8f; only event dates, water body and point depths.
source_inputs.water_quality: Pinned TBEP/EPCHC monthly water-quality table generated by analysis/02_water_quality_screen.py from wq-static commit 00aa86030f9245fe0318c186e7137798684dce74.

excluded_segments_reason: Boca Ciega Bay and Clearwater Bay are not represented in the frozen station-to-segment mapping of the current water-quality source; they are excluded before focal-response access.

visit_depth.rule: Median minimumDepthInMeters across eligible point events within each transect visit.

optical_transform.source_basis: The 1.7 Secchi-to-Kd relation is already used in Tampa Bay seagrass light-requirement work and is fixed here before focal-response access.
optical_transform.interpretation: Fraction of near-surface PAR remaining at the transect depth under the simplified Beer-Lambert proxy; not a directly measured canopy irradiance.

windows.primary: mean benthic-light fraction across the 6 complete calendar months before the survey month
windows.sensitivity: mean benthic-light fraction across the 3 complete calendar months before the survey month

next_gate: Only after this response-independent exposure preflight passes may a focal plant-condition outcome design be frozen.
claim_boundary: This exposure proxy combines segment-level water clarity with visit depth; it is not node-specific optical monitoring.
Secchi-derived Kd is an approximation and ignores spectral effects, epiphytes, canopy self-shading and bottom reflectance.
No focal biological response is opened or modeled in the preflight.
